title: Janapada of Aśmaka
capsule: Aśmaka (also Asmaka or Assaka) was one of the sixteen Mahājanapadas of ancient India, distinguished as the only one situated in the Deccan rather than the Gangetic plain, straddling the Godavari River in the region of present-day Telangana and Maharashtra. Its capital Podana (modern Bodhan) is mentioned in early Buddhist sources including the Anguttara Nikaya. By around 400 BCE the polity had been absorbed into the expanding Nanda Empire, disappearing as an independent unit. Its southerly location made it a cultural bridge between the Vedic north and Dravidian south.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Textual attestation from Buddhist Pali sources is good for the existence and capital of Aśmaka, but territorial extent is inferred from fragmentary references and remains schematic.
